rulings.dispute: O1 — shape, states and lifetime of the per-session config holder. Critic, readiness, structural, zoom-out, codebase, comprehension: a holder distinct from `TaiknrConfig` with states so a rejected file is never representable as `enabled:false`; critic/readiness want three states (unresolved | rejected | ready), catalyst two (inactive | ready), structural four (adds user-off). My orientation left in-place fill of the shared `TaiknrConfig` as an option.
rulings.answer: Three states, one holder, created per factory call. The holder is a new unit in `src/app/extension/` (the composition root already owns per-session ephemeral state per ARCHITECTURE §3) with the state union `unresolved` (from factory time until the first `session_start`) | `rejected` carrying the `TaiknrConfigError` | `ready` carrying the resolved `TaiknrConfig`. `enabled` is a field of the ready config, not a fourth state (structural's user-off collapses into ready+enabled:false). Three operations: assign the whole state once per `session_start` (ready or rejected; whole replacement, so a fixed file clears a prior rejection), `isActive()` = ready && config.enabled, and `setEnabled(boolean): boolean` that returns false and changes nothing unless ready — that is the Status card's seam. In-place fill of the shared `TaiknrConfig` is rejected: it cannot carry 'rejected', and it needs an initial value that is the defaults Joel's Q1(b) forbids running on. The holder is never module-level: Pi's loader caches the *factory* and re-runs it on every load, so module state survives session replacement while a factory-local holder does not. The in-session `setEnabled` flip therefore lasts until the next `session_start`, where the files are re-read. The design names the unit; two-state (catalyst) is rejected because the rejected state must carry the error for the seam's refusal message and the Status card's readout.
rulings.decided_by: Joel's Q1(b) (owner-rulings 'Orientation Q1': no fallback to defaults, closed until fixed) plus measurement of Pi 1.5.2 `dist/core/extensions/loader.js` L470–500: `loadExtensionModule` caches and returns the module factory; `initializeExtension` (L519) runs the factory on every `loadExtension`, so a new extension instance exists per session replacement and only module-level state leaks.
rulings.evidence: Read `loader.js` L462–500 and L519–560 myself: `extensionCache.set(extensionPath, factory)` stores the factory; `loadExtensionsInternal` → `loadExtension` → `initializeExtension(factory, …)` runs it each time. `agent-session.js` L2756–2779: `bindExtensions` binds `onError` then awaits `emit(session_start)`. At HEAD `taiknr.ts:19` pins `DEFAULT_TAIKNR_CONFIG` by value into turn-end and context deps; no value of `TaiknrConfig` means 'do nothing'.

rulings.dispute: How trust reaches the loader given the frozen `ConfigPaths { agentConfigPath: string; projectConfigPath: string }`. Critic CR-2, readiness R1, structural STR-1, zoom-out ZO-1, catalyst CAT-2, comprehension CC-6: make `projectConfigPath` optional (or an ordered path list) and never read an untrusted file; my D9 said `ConfigPaths` stays as at HEAD.
rulings.answer: `ConfigPaths` becomes `{ agentConfigPath: string; projectConfigPath: string | undefined }` — the key stays required so the caller must state the trust decision; `undefined` means 'no project layer'. The session-start handler sets it to the project path only when `ctx.isProjectTrusted()` is true; the loader never opens, parses or validates a file it is not given. An ordered path list is rejected: the deferred env layer is not a file path, and named fields are the clearer contract. This is a narrow revision of my D9 (which froze `ConfigPaths` as at HEAD) and the design records it as such. It does not need an entry in the `extension-packaging` delta: that clause governs `register*Handler` signatures and the adapter/port contracts, and `ConfigPaths` is neither. The `configuration` spec's 'SHALL receive both paths' is reworded to 'the agent path and the project path or `undefined`', and gains the scenario 'an untrusted project file that is malformed is never read and causes no rejection'.
rulings.decided_by: Pi `docs/extensions.md` L1197–1201 (`ctx.isProjectTrusted()`: 'Use this before reading project-local extension configuration'), S4, and the deletion test (nothing breaks with the optional layer; a sentinel path or a second loader would).
rulings.evidence: Re-read `docs/extensions.md` L1175–1201 and `src/config/taiknr-config.ts:15–18` at HEAD (both fields required strings). pi-jefferson `configuration.ts:365–369` reads the project path only when `source.projectTrusted && existsSync(projectPath)`, the same gate at the caller.

rulings.dispute: Structural's owner question: when a project is untrusted and its `pi-taiknr.json` is malformed, ignore it unread, or still reject the session under Q1(b)?
rulings.answer: Ignore it unread. Joel's Q1(b) was asked and answered about files taiknr reads; an untrusted project file is one taiknr must not read at all, so 'present but malformed' never arises for it. The security consequence is decisive: otherwise any repository the user `cd`s into can switch taiknr off for the session before trust is granted. This is the scenario added under the previous row; no question for Joel.
rulings.decided_by: Pi `docs/extensions.md` L1197–1201 (trust check precedes the read) and `docs/security.md` project-trust model; Joel's Q1(b) wording ('a present-but-malformed or invalid config file') scoped to files taiknr legitimately reads.
rulings.evidence: Read the docs lines myself; confirmed the ruling text in `owner-rulings.md` 'Orientation Q1'. Chidi Q1 and Eleanor §1 agree and neither was relied on without the source check.

rulings.dispute: O6 — where the inertness check lives. Critic CR-6, zoom-out, structural STR-3: one shared predicate called first in each handler body. Readiness R4, catalyst CAT-1: one gating Proxy over `pi.on` in the composition root for the six non-session-start registrars. Comprehension CC-5: whichever, session_start must be exempt and consumers must read current state.
rulings.answer: One gate at the composition root, as a small named function in `src/app/extension/` that wraps `pi.on` so a registered handler runs only while `holder.isActive()`; the six non-session-start registrars receive the gated `pi`, `registerSessionStartHandler` receives the raw `pi`. The decisions in play decide it: four of the six registrars (`session_tree`, `session_compact`, `tool_call`, `agent_before_settle`) have no config parameter, so a per-handler predicate forces a signature change in each later card, against D6/AGENTS.md ('the public signatures are fixed for the cards implementing behind them') and the delta's 'six registrars unchanged' clause; the gate changes none and is the only option testable now (Trap 12). Measured: the gate type-checks with one typed cast over Pi's overloaded `on`, Biome is clean, the entry test stays green because the fake is touched only through `on`, and the wrapper returns `undefined` while inactive and the handler's result once active (so an inactive `tool_call` neither blocks nor rewrites). The design records the cast as the one place the host's `on` typing is bypassed, and the rule that handlers read the holder at event time and never capture a `TaiknrConfig` at factory time. The session-start handler is the one body with an explicit `isActive()` call, in front of the hydration slot a later card fills. Later cards add no per-handler checks.
rulings.decided_by: D6 / AGENTS.md signature rule plus measurement in a `git archive HEAD` copy under `mktemp -d` (removed): `tsc --noEmit` exit 0 with `(target.on as On)(event, wrapper)`, `biome check src tests` clean, vitest 3 files / 5 tests green including the unchanged entry test; a direct run of the wrapper gave `undefined`/no call while inactive and the handler's `{ok:true}` once active.
rulings.evidence: First attempt without the cast failed `TS2769: No overload matches this call` (Pi's `on` has only per-event overloads, `types.d.ts` L1231–1266, no `event: string` catch-all); the cast form passed. Entry test's Proxy fake throws on any member other than `on`, and the gate's `Reflect.get` forwards only on access, so the test's 'touches nothing else' guarantee holds.

rulings.dispute: O3 / CC-2 — how a rejection surfaces in every mode. Critic: a throw from `session_start` after the holder is set reaches stderr in print and JSON modes, `extension_error` in RPC, the chat in TUI (source-read); comprehension and catalyst: JSON mode unverified and may corrupt the protocol stream.
rulings.answer: The report is one `Error` thrown from the session-start handler after the holder is set to `rejected`, and nothing else (no `ctx.ui.notify`). Measured live in Pi 1.5.2 with a throwaway extension whose `session_start` throws: `pi -p` printed `Extension error (<ext path>): <message>` on stderr; `pi --mode json` printed the same line on stderr while stdout carried only the `{"type":"session",…}` record, so the JSON protocol stream is untouched. Source confirms TUI (`interactive-mode.js` `showExtensionError`) and RPC (`rpc-mode.js` L267 `extension_error`). Order inside the handler: build paths from `ctx` → `loadTaiknrConfig` in try/catch → assign the holder (ready or rejected) → rethrow on rejection → hydration slot (later card) only when `isActive()`. The message is `<absolute file path>: <field>: <reason>` or `<absolute file path>: <reason>` when no field applies, ending with the recovery line 'fix the file, then run /reload or start a new session' (closes CC-1). The host already prefixes the extension path, so no `pi-taiknr:` prefix is required.
rulings.decided_by: Live measurement of Pi 1.5.2 print and JSON modes in a `mktemp -d` agent dir with `env -i` (no credentials, no model call: the run stopped at 'No API key found'), plus `print-mode.js` L86, `rpc-mode.js` L267, `agent-session.js` L2772–2776 (onError bound before `emit(session_start)`).
rulings.evidence: Throwaway `agent/extensions/thrower.ts` registering `session_start` that throws; `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR=$A HOME=$T pi --no-session -p "hi"` and `--mode json`: both stderr lines began `Extension error (/…/thrower.ts): pi-taiknr: /tmp/x/pi-taiknr.json: decisionThreshold: must be <= 1`; JSON stdout was one session record only. Exit code 1 came from the missing API key, so no exit-code claim is made for the extension throw. Temp dir removed.

rulings.dispute: The MODIFIED `extension-packaging` block contradicts itself (critic CR-3; structural STR-4 adds that 'exactly the ones the design names' is circular): it allows 'config-carrying dependency types' to change while also saying no registrar other than session-start may change types, and turn-end and context are among those six.
rulings.answer: Confirmed by reading the delta. The requirement and scenario are rewritten to enumerate the permitted differences by name: (1) `registerSessionStartHandler` gains the holder (and keeps `_pi` and the store); (2) the `config` member of `registerTurnEndHandler`'s and `registerContextHandler`'s deps objects changes type from `TaiknrConfig` to the holder; (3) the `ConfigPaths.projectConfigPath` type (recorded under D9, listed here for the reviewer's one list). Everything else — the other four registrars' full signatures, turn-end's and context's other members, `createPiJevScorerAdapter(ctx, config: TaiknrConfig)`, the ports — is unchanged against HEAD. The scenario compares the diff with that list, not with 'what the design names'; the design holds the exact before/after types once and the spec cites the list by member.
rulings.decided_by: One fact, one place, and the measurability requirement for a gated scenario (first change's precedent: 'Signatures unchanged' compared with HEAD mechanically).
rulings.evidence: Read `specs/extension-packaging/spec.md` in the change: requirement says 'No other registrar's … types MAY change' while permitting 'the config-carrying dependency types' to change; `turn-end.ts:6–13` and `context.ts:7–14` at HEAD are the carriers. STR-4's circularity is real because `design.md` does not exist yet.

rulings.dispute: Edge case: a UTF-8 BOM. The spec lists a BOM-prefixed object as unparsable (from my Trap 7); critic CR-4: Pi strips the BOM before every JSON config read it does, so rejecting it is stricter than the host on the same kind of file.
rulings.answer: Strip a leading U+FEFF before `JSON.parse`; a BOM-prefixed `{}` is valid. Trap 7 recorded a Node fact, not a contract; the host's own convention is the closest community practice under D2. `""` and `" "` stay rejections. The test row flips to 'accepted'. One line, no Pi import.
rulings.decided_by: Joel's standing community ruling (D2) applied to Pi's own practice: `stripBom(readFileSync(…))` before `JSON.parse` in `settings-manager.js` L269 and L452, `extensions/mcp/config.js` L48 and L180, `config.js` L466/L480, `resource-loader.js` L39, `pi-manifest.js` L9, `migrations.js` L30/45/144, `package-manager-cli.js` L37, `interactive-mode.js` L1095.
rulings.evidence: `rg stripBom` over Pi 1.5.2 `dist/` myself: 13 read sites; measured `JSON.parse("\uFEFF{…}".replace(/^\uFEFF/, ""))` parses on Node 26.8.1.

rulings.dispute: Edge case: a present but unreadable file — dangling symlink (critic CR-5), EACCES/EISDIR (readiness R3, comprehension CC-4, comprehension's owner question): absent, or broken under Q1(b)?
rulings.answer: Broken. Only a path with no directory entry is 'absent': read with try/catch; on `ENOENT` run `lstatSync` — if that also fails with `ENOENT` (or the read failed `ENOTDIR`, i.e. `<cwd>/<CONFIG_DIR_NAME>` is not a directory) the file is absent and silent; if `lstat` succeeds the entry is a dangling symlink and it is a rejection naming the file. `EISDIR`, `EACCES` and every other read error are rejections naming the file (no field) with the errno in the reason. Joel's Q1(b) rationale decides it: he chose closed over open so taiknr never runs on values the user did not choose; a config the user put in place that cannot be read is exactly that case, and his `~/.pi/agent` is dotfile-managed, where a link target can go missing. Not a question for Joel: the ruling's reason covers it.
rulings.decided_by: Joel's Q1(b) and its stated reason (owner-rulings 'Orientation Q1'); measurement of Node 26.8.1 errno behaviour.
rulings.evidence: Measured in a `mktemp -d` dir (removed): missing file → read `ENOENT`, lstat `ENOENT`; dangling symlink → read `ENOENT`, lstat ok (isSymbolicLink); directory → read `EISDIR`, lstat ok; path through a regular file → read `ENOTDIR`, lstat `ENOTDIR`. So `existsSync`-then-read cannot tell the first two apart; the lstat step can.

rulings.dispute: Test locations and conventions: the `configuration` spec puts the trust gate and the `session_start` re-read 'with the recording fake at the composition root' under `tests/config/` (readiness R7, zoom-out ZO-3) and restates vitest/`.js`/mirror conventions the living `development-checks` spec and AGENTS.md already own (structural STR-5).
rulings.answer: Tests mirror the `src/` layer they exercise (D7; AGENTS.md; ARCHITECTURE §8): `tests/config/` holds only the host-free loader cases (layering, every rejection class, BOM, dangling symlink, EISDIR, edge values); the holder and the gate are tested under `tests/app/extension/`; the session-start handler (paths from a fake `ctx`, trust gate, assign/throw order, re-read on a second call with a different cwd) under `tests/infra/pi-event-handlers/`; the existing entry test is unchanged. A handler-capturing fake of `ExtensionAPI` with a `ctx` stub is needed by more than one file, so it has one home under `tests/` (not collected: the include is `tests/**/*.test.ts`; still linted and type-checked: `tests/**`), path the design's. The `configuration` requirement keeps only the config-specific coverage list and cites `development-checks` for conventions instead of restating them.
rulings.decided_by: D7 (living `development-checks` spec + AGENTS.md mirror rule) and one-fact-one-place.
rulings.evidence: `vitest.config.ts` include `tests/**/*.test.ts`, `biome.json` includes `tests/**`, `tsconfig.json` includes `tests/**/*.ts` (read at HEAD); `tests/app/extension/taiknr.test.ts` records event names only and cannot invoke a handler or supply a `ctx`.

rulings.dispute: `CONFIG_DIR_NAME` testability (readiness R5): the spec scenario 'WHEN CONFIG_DIR_NAME is a value other than .pi' cannot be driven from a test because it is an import-time constant; readiness wants a pure `resolveConfigPaths` in `src/infra/` with injected values. Related: the proposal leaves the path-resolution site as 'taiknr.ts or src/infra/'.
rulings.answer: The scenario is reworded to what is observable: 'the project path is built from the host's `CONFIG_DIR_NAME`, and `src/` contains no literal `.pi` or `~/.pi` path segment' (a source search), plus the agent-path scenario tested by pointing `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` at a `mkdtemp` dir (measured working under vitest in the orientation). No pure resolver module: it would exist only to make an unobservable scenario testable, so it fails the deletion test. The two `join` calls live in the session-start handler (`src/infra/pi-event-handlers/session-start.ts`), which already has `ctx.cwd` and `ctx.isProjectTrusted()` and is where the host value import belongs (S1: never in `src/config/`). The file name `pi-taiknr.json` is one exported constant in `src/config/taiknr-config.ts`, so it is not written twice.
rulings.decided_by: Measurement that `CONFIG_DIR_NAME` is `pkg.piConfig?.configDir || ".pi"` evaluated at module load (`config.js` L492), S1, and the deletion test.
rulings.evidence: Read `config.js` L490–516; orientation measurement: `getAgentDir()` returned `/tmp/fake-agent/pi-taiknr.json` under vitest with `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` set, so the agent-path scenario is testable without mocks; the config-dir scenario is not.

rulings.dispute: Unknown-key rejection and version skew (readiness R6): Q1b 'reject' makes every future field a break for teammates sharing a committed project file across versions; readiness wants the message to carry the installed version, a deprecation window for removed fields, and Migration Plan text.
rulings.answer: Joel's Q1b stands: an unknown key is a rejection naming the file and the key, with the reason 'unknown field'. No version string in the message: the manifest has no `version` (first change, Decision 9) and Pi's exported `VERSION` is Pi's, so there is nothing true to print. No deprecation window is designed now: it belongs to the card that removes a field, if one ever does. The design's Risks records the skew consequence (a newer shared project file stops an older taiknr until the file or the install changes) and the rollback note that a pre-loader version ignores the file, so `enabled:false` stops working on rollback. Documentation of 'field X requires version Y' is the publishing card's, when there is a version.
rulings.decided_by: Joel's 'Q1b, reject it' (owner-rulings 'Orientation Q1b and Q2'); `package.json` at HEAD has no `version` field; first change design Decision 9.
rulings.evidence: Read `package.json` at HEAD (name, type, pi, scripts, peer/devDependencies only) and the archived `design.md` Decision 9.

rulings.dispute: O2 — typebox vs hand-written validation. Zoom-out, critic CR-8, readiness R12, catalyst: hand-written. Chidi's sample is mixed; the brief asks that it be checked against Joel's community principle.
rulings.answer: Hand-written guards in `src/config/taiknr-config.ts`, as one per-field rule table next to the defaults. D2 does not decide it — Chidi's sample shows hand-written, zod and typebox all in use, and the one sibling that validates (pi-jefferson) does it by hand — so the deletion test does: typebox adds a `peerDependencies` entry, still needs a message formatter (its unknown-key output is two entries), and puts a host-mapped import inside the layer the spec requires to be callable with no Pi runtime. Pinned rules, with the measured edge cases as test rows: known keys checked with `Object.hasOwn`/a `Set` (so `toString` is rejected as unknown and `__proto__` — an own key after `JSON.parse` — is rejected, never spread); `decisionThreshold` `Number.isFinite` then `0 ≤ x ≤ 1` (`1e999` → Infinity → rejected; `-0` accepted); `minCharsToArchive` `Number.isInteger` then `≥ 0`; the two model fields strings with `trim().length > 0`; `enabled` `typeof === "boolean"`. One error class `TaiknrConfigError extends Error { filePath: string; field: string | undefined; reason: string }` exported from `src/config/`; the first violation found is reported (one field per error, smallest and sufficient); parse, root-type and read failures have `field` undefined (closes CB-3/CC-3: 'names the file, and the field where one applies'). Layering iterates the known-key list over the parsed objects, never spreads them. `package.json` is untouched.
rulings.decided_by: Deletion test against the `configuration` spec's 'Callable with no Pi runtime' requirement; measurement of the edge values.
rulings.evidence: Node 26.8.1: `JSON.parse('{"a":1e999}').a` → `Infinity`, `Number.isFinite` false, `Number.isInteger(1e999)` false; `JSON.parse('{"__proto__":{}}')` has own key `__proto__` (`Object.hasOwn` true) and spread keeps it; `"toString" in {}` true while `Object.hasOwn({}, "toString")` false. pi-jefferson `configuration.ts:32–128` validates by hand and rejects unknown options (L112). typebox 1.3.27 is in `node_modules` only transitively (undeclared).

rulings.dispute: O7 — should a valid `enabled:false` be announced at session start? Critic, readiness, zoom-out, catalyst: silent; comprehension: one mode-appropriate notice; codebase: log-only (no user-facing notice).
rulings.answer: I would choose silent: no output at session start when the resolved config is valid and `enabled` is false. Reasons: the user wrote the switch deliberately, and a notice on every `/new`, `/resume`, `/fork` and `/reload` is repeated noise for an opt-out; D10 (narrowed) gives the status readout to the Status card, so a notice here is UI that card owns; and a rejected file stays loud regardless (previous rows). Codebase's log-only option is not available: Pi has no extension log API and `console.*` draws over the TUI or lands on JSON mode's stderr, so 'log-only' is either nothing or a stderr line. The cost of silence, which Joel should weigh: a forgotten project-level `enabled:false` leaves taiknr doing nothing with no hint until the Status card ships. Options: (a) silent; (b) one `ctx.ui.notify(…, "info")` per session start when `ctx.hasUI` (invisible in print/JSON); (c) a stderr line in every mode. Product behaviour, so his.
rulings.evidence: Owner rulings cover what 'off' does (Q3 'everything stops') and the card boundary ('The /taiknr on|off command'), not what the user sees. `docs/extensions.md` L1175–1177: `notify` works only where `hasUI`; `rg 'console\.|log\(' src` at HEAD → nothing (no logging exists).

rulings.dispute: O5 — observability of the resolution (my orientation bar: log entry, decisions, outcome). Critic CR-9, readiness R9, codebase CB-4/CB-6, catalyst CAT-3: Pi has no log channel; success-path output would break 'neither file → nothing reported' and JSON stdout purity; several want a `ConfigResolution` record (paths, present, trusted, outcome) stored on the holder as pull state.
rulings.answer: This change emits nothing on success and nothing on absence (S2), and the rejection throw is the only emission. No `ConfigResolution` record: its only consumers in this change would be its own tests, and the Status card that would read it does not exist yet — a field with no consumer fails Derek's bar and the deletion test. The rejected state already carries the absolute path, field and reason, and the ready state carries the config; that is the observable state this change has. The design records two hand-offs: (1) 'present but untrusted project file, ignored' is indistinguishable from 'absent' in this change (CB-4), and the Status card decides what it exposes and adds the record then; (2) the orientation's O5 bar is met here by the rejection path alone, stated plainly, not by a log that has nowhere to go.
rulings.decided_by: S2 ('neither file exists → nothing reported'), the deletion test, and measurement that Pi offers no logging channel to extensions (no logger in `docs/extensions.md`; `console.*` corrupts TUI/JSON output; JSON mode's stdout carried only the session record in the live run).
rulings.evidence: Live JSON-mode run above: stdout was the single session record; stderr carried the extension error. `rg -n 'log' docs/extensions.md` finds no extension logging API; `src/` at HEAD has no console or logger call.

rulings.dispute: The command seam's contract and lifetime (critic CR-6, readiness R11, comprehension CC-1): a writable boolean is not enough — the in-memory flip is lost at the next session replacement, `/taiknr on` after off finds a stale or unhydrated store, and a fixed file plus `/taiknr on` without `/reload` must not un-reject.
rulings.answer: The seam is the holder's `setEnabled(boolean): boolean` (row 1), not a bare field. Its contract, recorded in the design for the Status card: it succeeds only in `ready` (so a fixed-but-unreloaded rejection stays closed until `/reload` or a new session, and the refusal is why the rejection message names the recovery step); its effect lasts until the next `session_start`, which re-reads the files (measured: a new extension instance per session replacement); it does not hydrate — turning on mid-session after hydration was skipped is the Status card's hazard to handle when it wires the command, since hydration itself lands with the archive card. Nothing else is built here.
rulings.decided_by: Joel's 'The /taiknr on|off command' (this change leaves the seam and registers no command) and Q1(b); `loader.js` factory-per-load measurement (row 1).
rulings.evidence: `docs/extensions.md` L376–392 lifecycle: `/new`, `/resume`, `/fork`, `/reload` → `session_shutdown`, replacement runtime, `session_start`; `loader.js` L470–500 caches the factory, not the instance.

rulings.dispute: Codebase CB-5: the proposal and spec say the session config reaches 'the turn-end and context handler dependencies and the scorer adapter', but `createPiJevScorerAdapter(ctx, config)` has no call site at HEAD, so the adapter clause is unassertable.
rulings.answer: Drop the adapter from this change's wiring requirement. The wiring requirement names the two deps members (turn-end, context) that receive the holder; the recall card constructs the scorer adapter inside the context handler with the holder's ready config, and its signature stays `(ctx, config: TaiknrConfig)` (row 5). The spec's 'every handler and adapter that needs a TaiknrConfig' becomes 'the turn-end and context handler dependencies'.
rulings.decided_by: Measurement at HEAD: no caller of `createPiJevScorerAdapter`; the gated-scenario rule that a SHALL without an observable has no test.
rulings.evidence: `rg -n createPiJevScorerAdapter src tests` → the definition in `pi-jev-scorer-adapter.ts:7` only.

rulings.dispute: Critic CR-10: the spec's behavioural 'off' scenarios ('a project file turns taiknr off for one project', 'stubs made before the switch stay stubbed') cannot be tested in this change because all seven handlers are no-ops, and nothing says which card verifies them.
rulings.answer: Keep the scenarios (they state Joel's Q3 contract) and mark each in the spec as 'verified by the archive and recall cards through the composition-root gate'. This change tests what exists: the holder's state for `enabled:false`, `rejected` and `unresolved` all make `isActive()` false; the gate does not invoke a registered handler while inactive and does once active (measured, row 4); the trust-gated project `enabled:false` resolves correctly. No test is written against an invented handler body.
rulings.decided_by: Trap 12 (no-op handlers) and the first change's precedent of recording deferral explicitly rather than claiming satisfaction (development-checks 'The import boundary is not lint-enforced in this change').
rulings.evidence: All seven handler bodies at HEAD are `_pi.on("<event>", () => {})`; the gate wrapper was measured returning `undefined` without calling the inner handler while inactive.

rulings.dispute: Structural STR-6: the seven-registration invariant funnels resolution, trust, reading, reporting, ordering against hydration and the holder write into the session-start handler — a god handler — and wants a separate `resolveSessionConfig` orchestration function.
rulings.answer: No separate orchestration function. After the rulings above the handler body is four steps: two `join`s from `ctx` and the host helpers, one `loadTaiknrConfig` call in try/catch, one holder assignment, one rethrow. Validation and layering live in `src/config/`, the state machine in the holder, the gate in the composition root; the handler is the thin bridge ARCHITECTURE §3 describes. The Status card's re-validation reuses `loadTaiknrConfig`, not the handler. A second function would be the only place with one caller and fails the deletion test; the design may extract one if the handler grows past those steps when the archive card adds hydration.
rulings.decided_by: Deletion test and single-responsibility placement already fixed by rows 1, 4, 10 and 12.
rulings.evidence: Counted the handler's responsibilities after the rulings; each non-trivial one (validation, state, gating) already has a home elsewhere.
